subject: Safelist verification + evidence pack for private endpoint egress
messages:
From: Acme Health SecOps <security@acmehealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: netops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: egress safelist + evidence for private endpoint

Hi Vivek,

We're finalizing firewall rules for the upcoming Private deployment and need a concise set of artifacts to complete our audit folder. Can you provide:  

- A definitive list of outbound IPs (and CIDR ranges) that Redwood's private endpoints will originate from (including control plane callbacks if any).
- Any FQDNs/SNI hostnames customers must allow (if your workload uses hostnames for TLS termination).
- A short statement of whether connections are initiated from the customer network to Redwood or from Redwood to customer (and any port ranges).
- Sample logs or a minimal audit pack we can attach to the change ticket (connection timestamps, source IP, destination, and TLS SNI if available).

Goal: provide this as an evidence pack so our netops team can approve the safelist change and the compliance team can sign off. We have an implementation window next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Maya Sen
Security Operations Lead
Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: egress safelist + evidence for private endpoint

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble an "egress evidence pack" and a concise one-page summary for NetOps. Quick clarifications before we pull the artifacts:  

1) Are you only permitting static outbound NAT IPs (customer allowing Redwood -> internet) or do you also want the control-plane callback IPs when the control plane reaches back into the VPC?
2) Does Acme prefer CIDRs grouped by function (control plane, data egress, metrics/healthchecks) or a single flattened list?

I'll attach the CSV of IPs and a network diagram in the next message. Plan: Olga will validate the IP set against our egress pool and Marissa will drop sample connection logs (sanitized). Expect a consolidated package by EOD.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: egress safelist + evidence for private endpoint

Vivek — answered inline for our internal record and for Maya if you want to forward:  

On 1) Control plane callbacks: our Private deployment model has two flows: the customer (private endpoint) initiates TLS sessions to Redwood's control plane for management (port 443) and to data endpoints for model inference. Control-plane callbacks to the customer's network are only used in limited on-prem hosting modes where a management agent is running behind a customer NAT — we call these "agent-initiated secure tunnels." For the Acme default VPC option, there are no unsolicited inbound connections from Redwood.

On 2) Recommend grouped CIDRs by function for clarity. We'll provide 3 groups: control-plane (management), inference-data-egress (model serving), and telemetry/metrics (Prometheus push/health). Each group will include primary IPs and an ephemeral pool range for burst capacity.

Also: we'll include a note on SNI usage — we terminate TLS on Redwood's side; customers only need to allow outbound to the hostnames listed in the summary if they prefer hostname-based rules. IP-based safelist is preferred for strict netops environments.

I'll generate:
- redwood-egress-ip-list-20261019.csv (grouped, primary + ephemeral)
- private-endpoint-network-diagram-20261019.pdf (flow arrows, ports)
- short statement: "Connections are customer-initiated to Redwood; unsolicited inbound connections are not required for standard private endpoint deployments."
- sample logs: egress-audit-sample-logs-20261018.txt (sanitized)

Sending package now.

—Olga
Sr. Network Architect
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Acme Health SecOps <security@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Networking <netops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T14:01:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: egress safelist + evidence pack for private endpoint

Hi Maya / NetOps — attaching the egress evidence pack as discussed. Summary highlights below and attachments are in the Drive link at the bottom:  

Summary (one-paragraph): Redwood Private Endpoints are customer-triggered outbound TLS connections. For Acme's standard VPC deployment we recommend adding the three primary CIDR groups below to your outbound safelist. All connections are initiated from your VPC to Redwood on port 443 (SNI: redwood.private.redwood-inference.com when hostname rules are needed). There are ephemeral NAT IPs used for burst capacity; we provide both the stable primary IPs and the ephemeral range. No inbound traffic from Redwood to Acme is required for normal operation.

Primary CIDRs (grouped):
- control-plane: 34.200.16.0/28
- inference-data-egress: 34.201.32.0/27
- telemetry/metrics: 34.202.48.0/29

Ephemeral burst pool (please allow for this range to be used during scale events): 34.203.0.0/22

Attachments in this message: redwood-egress-ip-list-20261019.csv, private-endpoint-network-diagram-20261019.pdf, egress-audit-sample-logs-20261018.txt

Drive link (full evidence pack): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/AcmeHealth/egress-evidence-20261019

Next steps / ask for Acme:  
- NetOps: confirm you can schedule the safelist change during your maintenance window next Tuesday.
- Security: let us know if you need additional fields in logs (e.g., full X509 subject) or a signed statement for your audit binder.

If helpful, we can run a quick connectivity validation session (15–20 minutes) during the window and capture a live connection trace.

Best,
Vivek
